# PSC8 cartridge runtime (CP08)

PSC8 is the Z80 / Sega 8-bit engine installed at `0x086CA500` (must end before the Genesis runtime at `0x086E2000`).
The main collection PSI card launches **Phantasy Star I Retranslated v2.6.1** with YM2413 FM and persistent SRAM;
the Additional Content submenu launches Phantasy Star Adventure and Phantasy Star Gaiden in Game Gear mode.

## What changed in CP08

* **Assembly Z80 core** (`z80a.s`), generated by `core/gen_asm.py` (run `python3 core/gen_asm.py z80a.s`; it also
  writes `z80a.h`). Z80 registers live in ARM registers, flag lookups come from IWRAM tables, memory reads go
  through a 1 KiB page map, and hot handlers sit in IWRAM while rare/indexed/ED handlers stay in ROM. VDP data/control
  ports, the V counter and per-frame constant ports have assembly fast paths; idle polling loops end the CPU slice.
  It replaces `z80_gba.c` + the lost `z80_fast_spans.inc` (both kept only under `legacy/`).
* **Block audio**: PSG and FM are rendered in blocks with catch-up at every PSG/FM/stereo write (so timing is
  sample-accurate to the write), a 4-buffer output ring, ARM inner loops for steady FM operators (`fm_steady.s`)
  and PSG tones. PSG is not rendered at all while the FM unit mutes it.
* **YM2413 rhythm section** rewritten: key-on triggered drums with percussive decay, volumes from 0x36–0x38,
  BD on ch6, HH/SD on ch7, TOM/CYM on ch8.
* Event-driven multi-line CPU slices (line 192 / line-IRQ / frame end) instead of one slice per line.

No frame skip, cycle scaling or speed multiplier is used anywhere: guest time is exact, and if the GBA cannot keep up
the guest simply runs slower than real time.

## Build and test

```sh
python3 build.py                       # -> build/psc8.bin (build_cp08.py calls this and installs it)
gcc -O2 -DFM_STEADY_C -I. -o /tmp/fbt tests/fm_block_test.c fast_opll.c fast_opll_block.c && /tmp/fbt
                                       # FM/PSG block renderers == per-sample reference, bit-exact
```

`core/` holds the verification harnesses: `tests/zex.c` (ZEXDOC), `tests/lockstep.c` (lockstep against the
superzazu reference core in `vendor/z80`), `tests/smslock.c` (cartridge lockstep), `gbatest/` (runs every opcode on
the GBA through both the assembly core and the verified C core `z80f.h` and compares state; only `LD A,R` and DD/FD-ED
forms differ, both intentionally). `fmcmp/` (package `source/audits/fmcmp`) replays a captured PSI FM log through this
synth and emu2413 for comparison.

Config block at RAM `0x0203FF00`: {cartridge address, power-of-two size, flags (1 = GG, 2 = FM, 8 = persistent SRAM),
index}. PSI's 16 KiB SRAM bank maps to `0x0E004000..0x0E007FFF`. Heartbeat at `0x0203E000`: word 1 guest frames,
2 PC, 3 FM port writes, 4 GG port writes, 6 late frames.

Requires Clang/LLD/llvm-objcopy with ARM7TDMI support, Python 3; GCC for host tests. Override tools with
`PSC8_CC`, `PSC8_LD`, `PSC8_OBJCOPY`. Vendored MIT sources (superzazu/z80, emu2413) stay in `vendor/` as test oracles.
